steps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon butter and olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed saucepan over medium-high heat. Cook and stir onion in hot butter-oil until onion begins to turn golden brown at the edges, about 2 minutes. Pour in rice; stir until rice is coated in oil and has started to toast, 2 to 3 minutes.

Reduce heat to medium and stir in white wine. Cook until mostly evaporated, then stir in 1/3 of the boiling vegetable broth; continue stirring until incorporated. Repeat this process twice more, stirring constantly. Incorporating the broth should take 15 to 20 minutes total.

When rice is mostly tender, but still has a very slight crunch, stir in hearts of palm and Parmesan cheese until incorporated; season with salt and pepper. Cook for 1 more minute to heat through, then stir in parsley and remaining 1 tablespoon butter. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Hearts of Palm Risotto
raw_recipe.description: This hearts of palm rice recipe is a lovely vegetarian risotto with onion, white wine, and Parmesan for a delicious, subtle change from the norm.

review.reviewBody:
Sensational! This recipe rocks!
I got some help from a friend that says you can never stop stirring. I don't need to go to health club because my arms are so toned now. Used Artichoke hearts instead of hearts of palm.

I'm on a diet so I lightened it up a bit. I have made risotto many times so was sure cutting out some of the butter/oil wouldn't change it too much. I reduced the olive oil to one tsp, using this to saute the onion. I followed as directed except substituting Chicken for Vegetable Broth and using more broth instead of wine. I had a can of Hearts of Palm - used the entire thing diced fine (this may be too much for some but I love the taste!) Finally, topped with reduced fat Italian blend cheese. Delish - and it doesn't taste low fat!!

This was SO good! I used a non stick pan so that I didn't have to stir constantly. I stirred once every 2 minutes or so. I also added sliced portabella mushrooms when I added the hearts of palm. This was my first attempt at risotto - I will be making this recipe again!!!!

Really good! First time I had Palm hearts and they are delicious. I didn't have dry white wine. Substituted a suggestion of 30 ml white wine vinegar + 30 ml water. 

I also didn't have vegetable broth, so substituted with beef broth. The beef broth I have is commercially prepared and was too salty ...so in the end, it tasted great. I can imagine with the dry white wine and a nice light vegetable broth this would be so much better. I will try it again in the future. Maybe then I will take a picture.

We were looking for a way to jazz up rice as a side-dish and this did the trick! Out of necessity we used regular white rice (worked great), Sake for the white wine (it was all we had), added half of a can mushrooms (they added color and an extra layer of consistency), and omitted the cheese (just didn't have any). Even without the cheese, it was very thick and flavorful. Also followed another user's advice and stirred [almost] constantly. Thanks for the great recipe, this will definitely be a regular.

This is one of my favorite recipes! After the first time I made it, it was requested in my house the following two weeks. All three times, I served it with mahi mahi with a lemon sauce. The pairing is perfect. The only thing I did differently was use Italian herb Better than Bouillon rather than plain vegetable broth
delish! only made two changes...chicken broth instead of veggie and used garlic instead of onion(because I didn't have an onion). I added chopped mushrooms and chopped zucchini. Great family meal!

This is a tasty recipe. I used chicken broth instead of veggie and substituted mushrooms for the hearts of palm. Your instructions do not state when to add the cheese. I assume at the end as with most risottos.

I made this for a Christmas holiday dinner and it was fabulous! I scaled it to 6 servings and it worked fine.
Only change I made: I added about a cup of baby portabellos to the onion and sauteed them together.
Will definitely serve this again --- my next dinner party will be a hit with this on the side!

My toddlers loved it! I replaced, of course, the wine with more broth, and the broth was very light to avoid salt. A good way of making them eat hearts of palm, something unusual, and help them open up to a new taste.

I thought is recipe was good and fairly easy and could be made with ingredients I usually have. I used regular rice, used extra broth in place of wine, and skipped the parsley. There is stirring involved, so plan for that or have an assistant. Next time I will try to get all the ingredients. I bet it would be even better.
Made as written and this was great! A little fussy as risotto tends to be but great. I think mushrooms would have put it over the top and I will add them next time.
Great recipe
This was an easy recipe. I used Better than Bouillon Concentrated Vegetable Base and I think I used too much bc it was a little salty. Other than that, we really enjoyed it.

Meh, this was good but not amazing like I’d hoped for. I might make it again, but it’s not in the definite pile. Also not sure how the recipe picture turned out so white, mine was more golden brown.??
Great recipe. I've also made it with spinach instead of hearts of palm and it came out good. I'm about to make it with broccoli since that's what my mom is craving
Loved it, used chicken broth, but turned out amazing! So much savory flavor.
Delicious! All of my guests enjoyed it and couldn't wait for seconds. I added peas (like the description mentions) but otherwise followed the recipe.
Excellent recipe, not that hard to make. It has a very pleasant and delicate taste. Besides the Parmesan cheese, I also added some Gorgonzola cheese.
Almost tasteless. I would not make again.
